short: A massive British offensive that achieved the longest localized advance since trench warfare began, capturing Vimy Ridge.
full:
On 9 April 1917, British, Canadian, and Australian forces launched a major offensive near the French city of Arras to support the wider Nivelle Offensive further south. Following a meticulously planned artillery bombardment that heavily utilized counter-battery fire and a creeping barrage, the Allied infantry quickly overwhelmed the forward German positions. On the opening day, the Canadian Corps achieved a stunning victory by seizing the highly fortified escarpment of Vimy Ridge.

The rapid initial success pushed the front line forward by up to five miles, an unprecedented gain on the Western Front. However, logistical difficulties in moving artillery forward across the cratered battlefield prevented the Allies from capitalizing on the breakthrough. As German reserves arrived and established new defensive lines, the battle degenerated into a grinding war of attrition, eventually concluding on 16 May with staggering casualties on both sides but little further strategic gain.
